subject: Urban Planning
title: Parking Minimums: The Hidden Mandate
description: A micro-lesson that makes Parking Minimums: The Hidden Mandate usable.

hook.text: Most zoning codes require restaurants to build 10 parking spaces per 1,000 sq ft of floor area. It's the law.

buildup.text: Parking minimums were invented in the 1950s. Planners guessed how many spaces each business needed. The math was arbitrary.

discovery.text: Donald Shoup proved in 'The High Cost of Free Parking' that minimums waste land and raise prices for everyone.

twist.text: A church and a nightclub have different peak hours but the same parking requirement. The rules ignore reality.

climax.text: Cities across the US are eliminating parking minimums. Developers build what the market demands instead.

punchline.text: The parking lot is bigger than the building. Because the law says so.

quiz.question: Who proved that parking minimums are economically wasteful?
options: Jane Jacobs in 'The Death and Life of Great American Cities'
Donald Shoup in 'The High Cost of Free Parking'
